critiques.assumption: An agreed weekly manifest supplies sufficiently reliable intended-course truth to validate selection and reduce handling.
critiques.limitation: D1-O6 supplies heterogeneous references, while timetable completeness and update timing are unmeasured. Agreement with a manifest could therefore reproduce a shared omission. Fabricated fixtures establish behavior against stipulated truth, not the reliability of real manifests. This supports an evidence gap, not a finding that coordinators' schedules are wrong.
critiques.opening: Test reference disagreement and uncertainty explicitly before treating manifest confirmation as a correctness check.
critiques.comparison: Stable identity addresses renaming but cannot determine split-week membership. Coordinator reconciliation supplies week-specific intent but may be incomplete and costly. Their useful interaction requires explicit treatment of unresolved membership.
critiques.probe: Proposed only: inject stale-reference and split-course disagreements into fabricated tasks, including a case where both references omit the same intended course.

openings.claim: Use stable center-scoped identities with discrepancy-focused weekly reconciliation and an explicit unresolved-membership state.
openings.delta: Extend A1's confirmed manifest with reference provenance and unresolved decisions; prevent unresolved cases from being counted as verified usable exports. Include deliberately shared omissions in assessment.
openings.prediction: Relative to identity continuity alone, explicit decisions may resolve split and reassignment ambiguity. Relative to full coordinator reconciliation alone, identity matching may reduce repeated name checks. The interaction concentrates review on semantic changes. Failure boundary: jointly stale references can hide discrepancies; unresolved cases can increase handling or delay usable delivery.
openings.probe: Proposed, not performed: share the six coordinators' existing two-session budget across identity-only, reconciliation-only and combined fabricated tasks, counterbalancing order. Establish intended sets independently in task specifications. Measure correctness, unresolved cases and active handling; retain unresolved cases in outcome accounting. Test center isolation and concurrent attendance entry. First assess existing identifiers plus a minimal private prototype; stop expansion if six engineer-days or hosting allowance cannot hold. Subsequently measure the original next-40-export target.
assumptions: Processing remains private and the documented CSV remains supported.
Historical membership is not inferred from missing records.
Discrepancy detection does not establish reference completeness; fabricated results cannot establish field success.
